title: Analytics permission cache and consistent indexing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Analytics endpoints and per-route usage views sometimes return rows a user should not see because the per-tenant permission checks depend on live entitlement lookups that can be stale or expensive. Goal: Implement a permission-aware read-through cache and a consistent indexing scheme for analytics row visibility so dashboards and CSV exports enforce RBAC with low latency and predictable cost. This ticket covers schema-level index decisions, cache key format, invalidation hooks, a backfill to reconcile existing indexes, and an operational runbook for failures.
acceptance_criteria: All analytics read paths (dashboard API, CSV export, per-route usage endpoints) consult a unified permission index that reflects RBAC at request time
Read-through permission cache reduces median permission lookup latency by >= 40% for high-cardinality queries in staging
Cache invalidation events (user role change, tenant entitlement change, group membership update) propagate within 30s in staging and 60s in prod after rollout
Backfill script runs to populate indexes for all tenants older than 90 days and completes without row-level permission regressions
Automated integration test coverage for permission cache miss/hit, invalidation, and rollback scenarios
Operational metrics: cache hit rate, TTL churn, index freshness, and a Grafana dashboard with SLOs
implementation_notes: Design a permission index keyed by: tenant_id::resource_type::resource_id::permission_hash to allow selective scan avoidance
Use Redis for the read-through cache with short TTLs (default 60s) and a write-through hook to the index store on entitlement updates

Avoid expensive joins during query time by maintaining denormalized visibility markers at the analytics-materialized-table layer (daily incremental update + event-driven syncronization for near-realtime changes)
Backfill strategy: streaming backfill using a cursor-based job to avoid table locks; checkpoint every 1M rows; run in low-traffic window
Rollout plan: feature-flag the cache behavior per-route, start with internal/prod-readonly tenants, ramp to 25%/50%/100% over two weeks, monitor security alerts and cache metrics

Trade-offs considered: stronger consistency with immediate synchronous invalidation increases write latency vs eventual 30–60s window; chosen medium favors availability and cost with monitoring and fast invalidation where required (high-sensitivity tenants)
Security: all cache keys will be HMACed with service-level secret and tenant salt; index updates will be audited to the analytics-audit-log stream

migration_plan: Step 1: Create new index tables and tenant-facing visibility flags in analytics_materialized_views (no writes yet)
Step 2: Run streaming backfill to populate index for historical data; run with concurrency=4 and checkpoint after every 1M rows
Step 3: Enable event-driven syncer to keep index near-realtime for new events
Step 4: Flip feature flag for internal tenants; monitor metrics for 48h
Step 5: Gradually ramp feature flag to all tenants; enable export path to consult index
Rollback: disable feature flag and revert to legacy entitlement lookup; backfill will continue to run in read-only mode
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to cache key derivation and ensure HMAC uses tenant-specific salt
Evaluate trade-offs in the index schema: there is a space vs query-time cost choice; current design favors query speed
Verify integration test covers entitlement revocation and group membership propagation
